context: Read-only experiment; the deletion itself lands in Phase 1/2, not here. Anti-pattern: do not keep X11-in-sandbox because it happens to work - working is the worse outcome for the boundary.
description: Upstream mounts host /tmp/.X11-unix:ro into the container (run.sh:528-531). Two suspicions from review: (a) unix sockets bind-mounted across the virtiofs VM boundary generally do not work, so X11 mode is probably silently broken; (b) if it DOES work, a sandboxed agent holding the host display socket can capture screens and inject keys - a bigger hole than the network boundary closes. Test with XQuartz active via --shell and xdpyinfo against the mounted socket. DECISION RULE: broken -> delete X11 mode, keep Xvfb only; working -> delete it from sandboxed mode anyway (document as with-internet-only convenience at most). Either way record a Spike C verdict line.

preserves.behavior: No script changes from this spike
